about: Every state's and the District of Columbia's recount rules (automatic and requested), by kind of office, each read at the state's own code (or marked otherwise). A rule's quotation was verified word for word against the fetched text by pipeline/intake/state_law.py. Written 2026-11-07T07:52Z.

code.edition: Alaska Statutes 2025, as the Alaska Legislature's statutes page prints it

notes: Alaska's statute site (akleg.gov/basis/statutes.asp, print view by section range) answered with text for every page. elections.alaska.gov (the Division of Elections) was not used.

The earlier reader's lead for Alaska was confirmed for AS 15.20.530, 15.15.460 and 15.20.430-.450; the earlier note that any recount other than on a tie is on application stating a belief of mistake is also confirmed. New here: general elections are ranked-choice (AS 15.15.350), with a tie rule inside the count, and the open top-four primary has its own tie-for-fourth rule (AS 15.25.100).

threshold.conditions: only when two or more candidates tie for the highest number of votes for an office with one seat
threshold.in_words: only on a tie: the director initiates the recount

rules.cost_bearer: the state (no deposit is required where candidates received a tie vote)

sources.quote: If there is a tie vote as provided in [...] the director shall initiate the recount and give notice to the interested parties as provided in
The director shall immediately proceed with the recount of votes in the manner provided by
If the recount includes an office for which candidates received a tie vote, [...] the application need not include a deposit, and the state shall bear the cost of the recount.

rules.note: No other automatic recount in AS 15.20.430-15.20.530. Candidates tied in a primary: carried over by AS 15.25.090 [inferred].

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast for the two candidates for the contested office (for a question or proposition, the total votes in favor of or opposed to the issue)
threshold.conditions: the difference of 20 votes or less is inclusive; the percentage test is "less than .5 percent"; applies to the cost, not to the right to apply
threshold.in_words: a difference of 20 votes or less, or less than one-half of one percent of the votes for the two candidates (or for and against the issue): the application needs no deposit and the state pays

who_may_request: a defeated candidate, or 10 qualified voters, who believe a mistake was made in counting (application to the director)
rules.cost_bearer: the state (no deposit) within this margin

sources.quote: or the difference between the number of votes cast was 20 or less or was less than .5 percent of the total number of votes cast for the two candidates for the contested office, [...] the application need not include a deposit, and the state shall bear the cost of the recount.

rules.note: This is the margin at which a requested recount costs the applicant nothing; it does not make the recount automatic.

threshold.conditions: application within five days after the completion of the state review (three days for governor and lieutenant governor in the general election); it must state the basis of the belief that a mistake was made
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate or 10 qualified voters who believe a mistake was made may apply for a recount of any precinct or house district, with a deposit; no margin is required

who_may_request: a defeated candidate
10 qualified voters
rules.cost_bearer: the applicant, by deposit ($1,000 for each precinct, $2,000 for each house district, $15,000 for the entire state), refunded in full if a different candidate is declared elected or the recount vote for the applicant is four percent or more above the reported vote

sources.quote: A defeated candidate or 10 qualified voters who believe there has been a mistake made by an election official or by the counting board in counting the votes in an election, may file an application within five days after the completion of the state review to the director for a recount of the votes from any particular precinct or any house district and for any particular office, proposition, or question.

The application must include a deposit in cash, by certified check, or by bond with a surety approved by the director. The amount of the deposit is $1,000 for each precinct, $2,000 for each house district, and $15,000 for the entire state.

rules.note: The applicant must state in the application "the basis of the belief that a mistake has been made" (AS 15.20.440(a)); the statute names no margin.

threshold.percent_of: the winning and losing vote on the result contested
threshold.conditions: the two percent is only part of the cost test, as printed: the contestant pays all costs if the recount fails to reverse a result, or if the difference between the winning and losing vote is more than two percent
threshold.in_words: a recount of a municipal election demanded by a contestant is at the contestant's cost if it fails to reverse a result, or if the difference between the winning and losing vote is more than two percent (as printed, joined by "or")

who_may_request: a contestant of a municipal election (a voter; an election may be contested only by a voter, unless an ordinance says otherwise)
rules.cost_bearer: the contestant, if the recount fails to reverse a result or the difference is more than two percent (the text joins the two with "or"); who pays otherwise is not stated in the section

sources.quote: A contestant shall pay all costs and expenses incurred in a recount of an election demanded by the contestant if the recount fails to reverse a result of the election, or the difference between the winning and losing vote on the result contested is more than two percent.

rules.note: AS 29.26.070 is general law for municipalities; subsection (a) lets the governing body provide the time and procedure for a contest by ordinance, and (b)-(c) apply "unless otherwise provided by ordinance". Read as covering every municipal office [inferred]; ordinances and charters not read. The "or" in the cost sentence is copied as printed; whether the legislature meant "and" was not read.

Surprise: a tie for the state executive offices other than the Commissioner of State Lands is decided by the two houses of the General Assembly voting jointly; ties for Congress, the legislature and the Commissioner of State Lands go to a special runoff four weeks after the election; county and municipal ties go to a runoff, then a lot.

The guide also says (not recorded as a rule): a tie for second place is settled by lot at the county board, and the order of candidates' names on the ballot is determined by lot at a commission meeting.

threshold.conditions: petition to the county board of election commissioners for a recount of the returns from any precinct; due no later than two days after preliminary results if the outstanding overseas absentee and uncounted provisional ballots cannot change the result, otherwise before the final canvass or by noon on the seventh day after the election; one recount per candidate per election
threshold.in_words: any candidate dissatisfied with the returns may petition for a recount; no margin is required

sources.quote: Any candidate who is dissatisfied with the returns of the election may submit to the county board of election commissioners a petition requesting a recount of the returns from any precinct.

charge the candidate petitioning the recount up to a maximum rate of twenty-five cents (25¢) per vote cast in the precincts where the recount is requested or a total of two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for the entire county, whichever is less.
If the recount changes the outcome of the election, the cost shall be refunded to the candidate.

Surprise: the state executive offices (governor and the other five of the executive department) are decided by a joint ballot of the two houses on a tie, not by lot; every other office read is decided by lot, and a tied ballot issue is deemed to have failed.

threshold.percent_of: the number of votes cast for both such candidates or on such measures or proposals
threshold.conditions: the margin is between the two candidates receiving the greatest number of votes for the office, or between the votes for and against initiated or referred measures or proposals to amend the Constitution; not for precinct committeemen, school district governing boards, community college district governing boards, fire district boards or fire district chiefs or secretary-treasurers, or boards of other special districts
threshold.in_words: a margin of one-half of one percent or less of the votes cast for the top two candidates (or for and against a state-level measure): the recount is required

rules.cost_bearer: the state for an office filled by state electors or an initiative, referendum or constitutional measure; the county for a county or subdivision office; the city or town for a city or town office

sources.quote: A recount of the vote is required when the canvass of returns in a primary or general election shows that the margin between the two candidates receiving the greatest number of votes for a particular office, or between the number of votes cast for and against initiated or referred measures or proposals to amend the Constitution of Arizona, is less than or equal to one-half of one percent of the number of votes cast for both such candidates or on such measures or proposals.

Subsection A of this section does not apply to elections for precinct committeemen, school district governing boards, community college district governing boards, fire district boards or fire district chiefs or secretary-treasurers or boards of other special districts.

When the canvass shows that a recount is required, the secretary of state, within twenty-four hours after the last county canvass or the last day for county canvasses prescribed by section 16-642, whichever is earlier, shall

The expenses of the recount of the votes as provided in this article, if for an office to be filled by state electors, or if upon an initiative or referendum measure, or proposal to amend the constitution, shall be a state charge, and if for an office to be filled by the electors of a county or a subdivision of a county, or precinct, shall be a county charge.

rules.note: The recount is ordered by the superior court after the secretary of state (or the board of supervisors, or the city or town council) certifies the facts (16-662, 16-663); it is automatic in that no one requests it. Measures: only initiated or referred measures and constitutional amendments are named; whether other ballot issues (for example local bond questions) are covered was not read. Which office kinds are "state electors" for cost is read from the section's words. City and town offices: the expense is a city or town charge (16-666, second sentence). Presidential electors are not named; whether the 0.5 percent test applies to them was not read. A.R.S. 16-661 to 16-667 provide no recount on request; election contests are a separate article (16-667 says the article supplements, and a contest abates a recount).

The guide says: "There is no provision in California law to require an "automatic" recount in any election contest." That is the guide's statement, not read in the Code. So California has no automatic recount at a margin or a tie, and every recount is on a voter's request and at the requester's cost.
The earlier reader's report did not cover California.

notes: Colorado's General Assembly publishes the whole Title 1 as one PDF (olls.info, linked from its 2026 CRS download page); it answered with text.

Surprise: the automatic recount runs at one-half of one percent of the highest vote, and the same threshold applies to local nonpartisan elections; a tie for governor and lieutenant governor, secretary of state, treasurer or attorney general goes to a joint ballot of the two houses, while the lot is cast by the secretary of state for the other offices.
A primary tie between candidates of the same party for a non-county office is first left to the candidates to settle by agreement (C.R.S. 1-11-101(3)).

threshold.percent_of: the highest vote cast in that election contest (for a contest with more than one person to be elected, the votes cast for the candidate who won with the least votes)
threshold.conditions: the recount occurs only after the canvass board certifies the original count; a political subdivision that referred a ballot issue or question to the electors may waive the automatic recount if the issue or question fails, by written notice within twenty-three days after the election (C.R.S. 1-10.5-103)
threshold.in_words: a difference between the highest and the next highest vote of one-half of one percent or less of the highest vote: a recount is held

rules.waiver: a political subdivision that referred a ballot issue or ballot question may waive the automatic recount if the issue fails, by written notice to the county clerk and recorder within twenty-three days after the election; no waiver by a candidate is stated
rules.cost_bearer: the entity that certified the candidate, ballot question or ballot issue for the ballot

sources.quote: A recount of any election contest shall be held if the difference between the highest number of votes cast in that election contest and the next highest number of votes cast in that election contest is less than or equal to one-half of one percent of the highest vote cast in that election contest.

If there is more than one person to be elected in an election contest, a recount shall be held if the difference between the votes cast for the candidate who won the election with the least votes and the candidate who lost the election with the most votes is less than or equal to one-half of one percent of the votes cast for the candidate who won the election with the least votes.
any expenses incurred in conducting a recount in any political subdivision shall be paid by the entity that certified the candidate, ballot question, or ballot issue for the ballot.

A political subdivision that referred a ballot issue or ballot question to the electors may waive the automatic recount provisions of this section if the ballot issue or ballot question fails by giving written notice to the county clerk and recorder within twenty-three days after any election.

rules.note: C.R.S. 1-10.5-101(1)(b) and (2) and 1-10.5-103. The secretary of state orders the recount for U.S. Senate and House, state offices, district offices of state concern and state questions (1-10.5-102); the county clerk and recorder for the rest in an election the clerk coordinates (1-10.5-103). "Any election contest" is read as including primaries (1-11-101(3) speaks of ties "after all recounts have been completed" in a primary, and 1-10.5-106 names primary elections).

Surprise: in Delaware a tie in a general election is not settled by a lot at all in the sections read: the court certifies a vacancy, and a vacancy in the General Assembly or in the House is filled by a special election; a municipal tie is a new election run by the State Election Commissioner; a primary tie goes to the party's committee.
Delaware's automatic recount thresholds are the lesser of 1,000 votes and one-half of one percent of the two candidates' votes, which is mainly the percentage for any race under about 200,000 votes.

The PDFs break words with hyphens at line ends, so quotations are taken from the section pages except 34-2302, whose quoted words are not broken.
Idaho has no automatic recount in the sections read; every recount is on request. Ties are settled by a toss of a coin.

threshold.conditions: for a measure, the difference between the yes and no votes; request in writing, filed with the appropriate officer within twenty days of the canvass (34-2301)

sources.quote: A losing candidate for nomination, or election or person supporting or opposing a ballot measure, may request a recount of the votes cast for the nomination or election to that office or passage or failure of a measure if the difference between the vote cast for that candidate and for the winning candidate for nomination or election, or the difference between the yes and no votes on a measure, is less than or equal to one-tenth of one percent (0.1%) of the total votes cast for that office or five (5) votes, whichever is greater.
The state shall pay for the recount of a federal, state, or legislative district office, or state measure while the county shall pay for the recount of a county, city or district office or measure.

rules.note: Called the 'free recount' in the section's heading. It is on request, not automatic: no recount happens in Idaho without a request in the sections read. For a measure the text compares yes and no votes with '0.1% of the total votes cast for that office or five votes', so the percentage's base for a measure is not stated [as written].

threshold.conditions: application within twenty days of the canvass: to the attorney general for federal, state, county or municipal office or a state, county or city measure; to the county clerk for all other offices and measures; the requester states the precincts and remits $100 for each; to be relieved of costs the requester must ask for at least 20 precincts with 5,000 votes (federal or state office or measure), 5 precincts with 1,250 votes (state legislative district), 2 precincts with 500 votes (county office or measure), or 2 precincts with 200 votes (city or district elections)
threshold.in_words: any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office, or any person supporting or opposing a measure, may apply for a recount of chosen precincts at $100 a precinct, whatever the margin

who_may_request: any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office desiring a recount
a person supporting or opposing a state, county or city measure
candidates for all other offices and supporters and opponents of all other measures (to the county clerk)
rules.cost_bearer: the requester ($100 per precinct), unless the recount shows a difference that, projected across all the precincts of the office, would change the result in the requester's favor: then the county or state bears the cost, the money is returned, and a general recount of the remaining precincts is required (34-2307, in the chapter PDF)

sources.quote: Any candidate for federal, state, county or municipal office desiring a recount of the ballots cast in any nominating or general election or person supporting or opposing a state, county or city measure, may apply to the attorney general therefor, within twenty (20) days of the canvass of such election
the sum of one hundred dollars ($100) for each such precinct in which he desires a recount made.

If the results of the recount indicate a difference, which if projected across all the precincts of the office in question would change the result of the election in favor of the candidate requesting the recount or change in the measure being recounted, then the cost of such recount shall be borne by the county or state
shall require a recount to be made in all the remaining precincts of the office in question.

rules.note: No margin condition is stated in 34-2301 or 34-2302 [as written]; the rule is read as available whatever the margin, at the requester's cost, and the cost is refunded if the recount shows a result-changing difference.

Surprising rules: there is no automatic recount at any margin; a primary tie is a candidate vacancy filled by party caucus; a general election tie for an office other than governor and lieutenant governor is a special election; a tie for governor or lieutenant governor goes to the General Assembly in joint session; a local tie is settled by the local fiscal body electing a person.

file a bond or cash deposit of at least $100 with the court for payment of costs of the recount. For every precinct over ten to be recounted, the bond or cash amount should be increased by $10 per precinct or $100 per precinct, depending upon whether the candidate lost by more or less than 1%.
If the recount petition is successful, the petitioner’s deposit or bond is refunded in full.

threshold.conditions: written request filed with the county election officer not later than 5 p.m. on the day following the last meeting of the county board of canvassers; the request names the voting areas to be recounted; the recount is completed by 5 p.m. on the fifth day after the request; the requester files a bond (security approved by the county or district attorney) conditioned to pay all costs incurred by the county

the party who makes the request shall file with the county election officer a bond, with security to be approved by the county or district attorney, conditioned to pay all costs incurred by the county in making the recount.

The earlier reader's lead (research/historical-close-races-v2.md 3a and 3b) is borne out: lot for a tie (118.425(6)) and an automatic recount at not more than one-half of one percent (120.157, effective June 29, 2021); it also gave 'requested, no margin, with a bond' (120.185), confirmed. New here: the recanvass at under one percent (117.305), and the automatic recount covers only the offices it lists, not primaries or local offices.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast for the office
threshold.conditions: applies to members of the General Assembly, the U.S. Senate and House, Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Commissioner of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics, Secretary of State and Attorney General; the State Board of Elections determines whether a recount is required from the total votes certified to the Secretary of State; the county boards of elections conduct it
threshold.in_words: a candidate defeated by a margin of not more than one-half of one percent of the votes cast for the office makes a recount mandatory

who_may_request: no request: required by the statute
rules.cost_bearer: the Commonwealth of Kentucky

sources.quote: In any regular election or special election for any member of the General Assembly, the United States Senate or the United States House of Representatives, Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Treasurer, Auditor of Public Accounts, Commissioner of Agriculture, Labor and Statistics, Secretary of State, and Attorney General, a recount of the vote shall be required when a candidate is defeated by a margin of not more than one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the votes cast for the office.
The costs of any recount held pursuant to this section shall be paid by the Commonwealth of Kentucky.
The State Board of Elections shall determine whether a recount is required under this section based upon the total number of votes certified to the Secretary of State.

rules.note: 'Not more than' is inclusive. The section lists the offices; the presidency, other statewide offices not listed, local offices, primaries and public questions are not covered by it. It dates from 2021 Ky. Acts ch. 197 (effective June 29, 2021).

threshold.in_words: a candidate who is not entitled to the automatic recount may petition the court for a recount whatever the margin, on a bond for the costs

Any candidate for the General Assembly who was voted for at a regular election or special election, and who does not qualify for an automatic recount under KRS 120.157, may request a recount of the ballots by filing a petition in the Circuit Court of the county where the requesting candidate resides.
The party requesting the recount shall execute bond with approved surety for the costs of the recount, in an amount to be fixed by the Circuit Judge.

Louisiana has two systems at once since 2026: closed party primaries (with a second party primary) for Congress, the supreme court, BESE and the Public Service Commission, and the open primary followed by a general election for every other office. A tie rule is recorded for each.

Louisiana has no automatic recount and no margin-triggered recount in Title 18 as printed; a candidate (or, for a proposition, a voter) may ask for a recount of the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots only, at their own cost, when those ballots could change the result.

threshold.conditions: the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for all candidates for the office could make a difference in the outcome of the election for the office
threshold.in_words: no percentage or vote margin; a candidate for the office may have the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots recounted if those ballots could change who wins

who_may_request: a candidate for the office, in writing, filed with the clerk of court by 4:30 p.m. on the third calendar day after the election
rules.cost_bearer: the requesting candidate, who pays all reasonable costs when the request is filed; the clerk refunds the costs if the recount changes the outcome of the election, and they become a reimbursable election expense

sources.quote: if the number of absentee by mail and early voting ballots cast for all candidates for an office could make a difference in the outcome of the election for the office, upon the written request of a candidate for the office, the board shall recount the absentee by mail ballots by hand or scanning equipment and early voting ballots electronically
The candidate or the voter in the proposition election requesting the recount shall be responsible for all reasonable costs associated with such recount, which shall be payable to the clerk of court.

rules.note: R.S. 18:1313.1(K)(2) in the current text (the same words are in R.S. 18:1313(K)(2), the alternative procedure a parish board may elect). Only the absentee-by-mail and early-voting ballots are recounted under it; ballots cast on election day are on voting machines, which a candidate may have reopened for reinspection on written request at the candidate's cost (R.S. 18:573(A)(3)), and that is an inspection, not a recount. The statute names 'an office' and does not separate federal, state and local offices, so the kinds are read from that wording [inferred]. The whole of Title 18 as printed was searched for 'recount': there is no automatic recount and no recount keyed to a percentage or number of votes.

notes: Maryland's Election Law article has no tie-break for a general election for Congress, the electors or the legislature; ties are in the Constitution (Governor and Lieutenant Governor by the General Assembly with a lot as the last step; Attorney General by the Governor; Delegates and Senators by the party central committee and the Governor; other officers by a new election ordered by the Governor) and in a few Election Law sections (primary for a one-county office by the party central committee; boards of education).
Maryland has no automatic recount: every recount is on the petition of a candidate (or, for a question, of a registered voter) at a margin of 5% or less, free at 0.25% or less.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes cast for those candidates (the apparent winner and the losing candidate with the highest number of votes for the office)
threshold.in_words: a defeated candidate for public or party office may petition for a recount if the margin between the apparent winner and the leading loser is not more than 5% of the votes cast for those two

who_may_request: a candidate for public or party office who has been defeated on the certified results, by petition filed within 3 days after the results are certified; an opposing candidate may file a counterpetition if the petition did not cover all the precincts and the winner changes
rules.cost_bearer: the petitioner, whose bond is liable (the cost is the county's if the margin was 0.25% or less, the outcome changed, or the petitioner gained 2% or more)

sources.quote: a candidate for public or party office who has been defeated based on the certified results of any election conducted under this article may petition for a recount of the votes cast for the office sought.

A candidate may not petition for a recount if the margin of difference between the number of votes received by an apparent winner and the losing candidate with the highest number of votes for the office is greater than 5% of the total votes cast for those candidates.

rules.note: Election Law 12-101 (petition) with 12-102 (counterpetition), 12-105 (bond set by a circuit judge) and 12-107 (cost). The section covers "any election conducted under this article"; the kinds list follows that wording [inferred for presidential electors, not named]. The petitioner chooses the method (rescan, manual recount of voter-verifiable paper records, or another method the State Administrator approves) under 12-108. There is no automatic recount in the article (searched).

Minnesota's recounts are all on a written request (there is no automatic recount of a candidate race); the publicly funded ones are free to the candidate within the thresholds, and a constitutional amendment within one-quarter percent is recounted without a request.

threshold.conditions: the vote-count alternative (10 votes or less) applies only if 400 votes or fewer were cast for the office
threshold.in_words: a margin under one-half of one percent, or ten votes or less where 400 votes or fewer were cast

who_may_request: the candidate whose election is in question, in writing
rules.cost_bearer: jurisdiction (the manual recount is at no cost to the candidate within the thresholds)

rules.note: The board recounts manually on the candidate's written request; there is no recount without the request, so this is a requested recount that costs the candidate nothing, not an automatic one. Request due by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the canvass (204C.35 subd. 1(b)).

Missouri has no recount without a request, a contest or a petition by the election authority. The one margin rule is RSMo 115.601: one-half of one percent for those who filed with the secretary of state, to be requested within seven days after certification; one percent for a contestant whose contest is heard by a court. Section 115.575(1) nonetheless calls the 115.601 recount 'automatic'.

A tie is settled by a special election among the tied candidates only (the governor orders it for federal and state legislative offices, the officer with whom they filed for the rest), or by the general assembly for the six state officers and for electors, or by lot if every tied candidate agrees.

threshold.percent_of: the votes cast (for a question, the votes cast on the question)
threshold.conditions: the request must state that the person, or the person's position on a question, was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast
threshold.in_words: a candidate who filed with the secretary of state, or a person whose position on a statewide question lost, by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast, is allowed a recount on filing a request with the secretary of state

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, or the person whose position on a question was defeated, by a request filed with the secretary of state not later than seven days after certification of the election
rules.cost_bearer: not stated in section 115.601

sources.quote: the defeated candidate or the person whose position on a question was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast on the question shall be allowed a recount pursuant to this section by filing with the secretary of state a request for a recount stating that the person or the person's position on a question was defeated by less than one-half of one percent of the votes cast.
Such request shall be filed not later than seven days after certification of the election.
The secretary of state shall conduct and certify the results of the recount as the official results in the election within twenty days of receipt of the aforementioned notice of recount.
or for recount other than the automatic recount provided for in section 115.601

rules.note: RSMo 115.601.3 and .4. The secretary of state runs it with persons appointed equally from lists of the contestant and the opponent; 'recount' is defined as one additional counting of all votes counted for the office or on the question. Subsection 1 of the same section says 'less than one percent', the heading says 'one-half of one percent', and subsection 3 says 'one-half of one percent' for these filers; the subsection that governs these filers is 3, so 0.5 is recorded. Section 115.575(1) calls this 'the automatic recount', but 115.601.3 requires a filed request, so it is recorded as requested. Which offices file with the secretary of state is not stated in the sections read (115.349 says 'the appropriate election official'); the kinds listed are my reading from the offices whose abstracts go to the secretary of state (115.507.4) [inferred].

Mississippi has no recount in the Election Code as printed: no automatic recount, no recount on request. A candidate may examine the ballot boxes (23-15-911) and may bring an election contest within twenty days (23-15-921, 23-15-951) or thirty days for a legislative seat (23-15-955). The straw draw is unusual: since 2017 a tie for a district office, a seat on the Supreme Court or Court of Appeals is decided by drawing straws from an opaque bag, not by lot or coin.
The governor's tie rule, changed in 2020, is the main thing not read.

Montana's tie rules are the most varied of the nine: after a recount, a tie for Congress goes to a special election ordered by the governor; for a supreme court justice, district judge or legislator the governor appoints one of the tied; for statewide executive officers the legislature elects by joint ballot; county commissioner, other county and subdivision offices are filled by appointment of one of the tied; a primary tie is decided by lot. Every certified tie is recounted first.

Recounts are all on petition except the tie recount: a free recount at one-quarter of one percent (or 10 votes for local offices, whichever is greater), a recount at one-quarter to one-half of one percent if the candidate posts a bond, and a court-ordered recount on probable cause at any margin.

Nebraska's automatic recount margin is measured against the winning candidate's votes, not the total votes cast, and is one percent (two percent where 500 or fewer votes were cast).

sources.quote: (1) Any candidate who failed to be nominated or elected shall be entitled to a recount if it appears, as evidenced by the abstract of votes, that the candidate failed to be nominated or elected by one of the following margins: (a) If more than five hundred votes were cast for the office, one percent or less of the votes received by the candidate:
All expenses of a recount under this section shall be paid by those political subdivisions involved in the recount.

rules.note: The section is headed "Automatic recount" and the recount is made by the county canvassing board without a request, subject to the candidate's waiver. Its words are "any candidate" and it does not list offices, so the kinds are read as every office on a primary or general ballot [inferred]; the margin is measured from the votes of the winning (or last qualifying) candidate, not from the total cast. Section 32-1119(4) says recounts for candidates who filed with the Secretary of State are made on the fifth Wednesday after the election; other recounts are made by the county canvassing board after its canvass (32-1119(5)).

For the purposes of this section, the term margin of victory shall mean the margin between all votes cast in the entire contest following the recanvass of votes.

sources.quote: If the number of votes cast in any county or municipal election for the declared winning nominee, candidate, question, or issue does not exceed the number of votes cast for the declared defeated nominee, candidate, question, or issue by a margin of one-half of one per cent or more of the total vote, the appropriate board of elections shall order a recount

If the board of elections in a county orders a recount in any county or municipal election pursuant to section 3515.011 of the Revised Code, the expense of the recount shall be paid from the county treasury in the same manner as other expenses of the board under section 3501.17 of the Revised Code.

notes: Title 26 was read as one PDF (the legislature's documented download); the whole title was searched for the words tie, tied, by lot, recount and automatic, and chapter 8 (sections 26-8-101 to 26-8-122) was read in full.

Oklahoma recounts of candidate races have no margin condition and are at the petitioner's cost, so a recount does not by itself follow a close margin; there is no automatic recount for candidate races.

A tie is settled by lot at the election board's public meeting, except: a primary tie for first place among three or more candidates where a runoff primary is to be held (the tied names go on the runoff ballot), and elections of elective state officers, where the Constitution (Art. VI, section 5) has the Legislature choose by joint ballot.

threshold.conditions: a candidate whose name was printed on the ballot for that office in that election; the deposit is doubled if the margin between first and second place is ten percent or more
threshold.in_words: no margin condition: a candidate whose name was printed on the ballot may petition for a recount; the deposit is doubled when the margin between the first-place and second-place candidates is ten percent or greater

who_may_request: a candidate whose name was printed on the ballot for that office in that election (an individual 'authorized to request a recount' for a question or issue, see the measure rules)
rules.cost_bearer: the petitioner, by a deposit (cashier's or certified check) of $600 for each 3,000 ballots or fraction thereof per county for a manual recount, or $600 for the first 3,000 and $300 for each additional 5,000 for an electronic-device recount, $300 more if filed with the State Election Board; the deposit is used for the actual expenses and the balance returned; if the petitioner is successful the deposit is returned and the county or state bears the expense (section 26-8-117)
rules.waiver: none found; no deposit beyond the first is required in a Primary Election with three or more candidates where the second- and third-place candidates are less than one percent apart, or the first-place candidate is within one percent of a majority (section 26-8-111(A)(6))

sources.quote: For an election involving candidates, the petition shall be filed with the secretary of the election board with whom the candidate filed the candidate's declaration of candidacy, unless otherwise provided for by law. The petition may only be filed by a candidate whose name was printed on the ballot for that office in that election.

If the candidate or individual requests that the ballots be recounted manually, the petition must be accompanied by a cashier's check or certified check in the amount of Six Hundred Dollars ($600.00) for each three thousand (3,000) ballots or fraction thereof, to be recounted for each county affected.

In elections involving candidates, an additional deposit equal to the total of the deposits required by paragraphs 2, 4 and 5 of this subsection shall be required if the margin between the first-place candidate and second-place candidate is ten percent (10%) or greater.

In the event the contestant is successful in the recount, the deposit shall be returned to the [...] contestant, and the expense of the recount shall be borne by the county or state, as the case may be.

rules.note: No automatic recount for candidate races was found in Title 26 (the word 'automatic' occurs once, for state questions). Kinds are mapped from the words 'an election involving candidates' [inferred]. The additional (doubled) deposit is refundable only if the contestant changes the outcome (section 26-8-117).

notes: Pages were fetched once each from oregonlegislature.gov on 2026-11-07. The pages carry a few non-UTF-8 bytes (section signs and apostrophes) that the helper shows as replacement characters; the quotations avoid them.
Chapter 254 was searched for tie, by lot and equal number of votes; ORS 254.575 is the only tie provision found. Chapter 258 was read through (recount sections 258.150 to 258.300).

In Oregon a tie always triggers a full recount first (ORS 258.280(1)(a)); only if it persists does the lot (legislature, local, primary), a new election (federal, statewide other than governor, presidential electors) or the Legislative Assembly (governor) apply.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes for both candidates (the apparently elected candidate and the closest apparently defeated opponent)
threshold.conditions: the canvass reveals either that two or more candidates have an equal and the highest number of votes, or that the difference is not more than one-fifth of one percent
threshold.in_words: a tie, or a difference between the apparent winner and the closest apparently defeated opponent of not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes for both candidates

rules.cost_bearer: the county for a county office, the city for a city office, the special district for a special district office, the state for any other office

sources.quote: The Secretary of State shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to a public office for which the Secretary of State is the filing officer, and the county clerk who conducted the election shall order a full recount of the votes cast for nomination or election to any other public office if the canvass of votes of the election reveals that:

The difference in the number of votes cast for a candidate apparently nominated or elected to the office and the votes cast for the closest apparently defeated opponent is not more than one-fifth of one percent of the total votes for both candidates.

The cost of a full recount conducted under this section shall be paid by the county for a county office, by the city for a city office, by the special district for a special district office or by the state for any other office.

rules.note: 'Public office' and 'nomination' are not limited by kind in the text; the kinds list is a mapping [inferred]. Both triggers lead to a full recount ordered by the Secretary of State (offices it takes filings for) or the county clerk. The 'votes: 0' field records the tie alternative.

sources.quote: A candidate or an officer of a political party on behalf of a candidate of the political party may file a demand requiring the Secretary of State to direct that a recount be made in specified precincts in which votes were cast for the nomination or office for which the candidate received a vote.

each demand shall be accompanied by a cash deposit of $15 for each precinct to be recounted up to a maximum of $8,000 for a recount of all precincts in the state on a measure or for a nomination or office.

If the abstract of votes resulting from a full recount shows that the outcome of the election on the measure was changed or that a candidate for whose benefit the recount was demanded received a plurality of the votes, the deposit required by ORS 258.161 shall be refunded by the Secretary of State to the person who filed the demand.

rules.note: A partial recount does not change the official returns: the person demanding is bound by the original returns unless a full recount is demanded (ORS 258.171, not quoted). Only one recount is made per office (ORS 258.181, not quoted). Kinds are a mapping of 'nomination or office' [inferred].

Rhode Island has no automatic recount and no recount on a tie in the sections read: every recount is requested by a trailing candidate (or, for questions, a person of recognized standing) within a size-tiered margin, and a tie leaves 'no plurality' (new election for Congress and the general assembly), a vote of the general assembly (general offices), or a party committee (primaries).

South Carolina breaks a tie by a runoff two weeks later (not by lot) for general, special and primary elections, unless a candidate withdraws; the mandatory recount threshold is one percent of the votes cast for the office.

threshold.percent_of: the total votes which were cast for such office
threshold.conditions: the difference between the candidate declared nominated (primary) or elected (general) and any other candidate, or between the candidate who received the least number of votes to qualify for a runoff and a candidate who did not qualify
threshold.in_words: a difference of not more than one percent of the total votes cast for the office, between the declared winner and any other candidate, or at the runoff-qualification line in a primary

rules.cost_bearer: not stated in this section
rules.waiver: the other candidate or candidates may waive the recount in writing

sources.quote: Whenever the difference between the number of votes received by a candidate who has been declared nominated for an office in a primary election or who has been declared elected to an office in a general election and the number of votes received by any other candidate or candidate not declared so nominated or elected [...] shall be not more than one percent of the total votes which were cast for such office therein, the committee or board charged by law with canvassing such votes shall order a recount of such votes to be made forthwith unless such other candidate or candidates shall waive a recount in writing.

rules.note: The text says 'an office' and names no kind; the kinds are a mapping [inferred]. The recount is ordered by 'the committee or board charged by law with canvassing such votes' (the county board of canvassers or the Board of State Canvassers; for a primary the party committee). The quotation is cut at the runoff-qualification clause. A tie is a difference of zero and so falls within the rule; no separate tie-recount rule was found.

South Dakota recounts a tie automatically and then, if still tied, draws lots (state and county offices); in municipal and school elections a tie goes to lots after an optional recount.

threshold.conditions: a tie vote on the canvass of the original official returns that makes it impossible to declare who has been elected or nominated; does not apply to school and township elections
threshold.in_words: a recount of all the votes involved happens when the canvass shows a tie

sources.quote: Thereupon such county auditor or such secretary of state, as the case may be, shall proceed exactly as if a petition had been duly filed under §§ 12-21-7 to 12-21-15, inclusive, requiring a recount to be made of all votes [...] involved, and such recount shall proceed accordingly. This section shall not apply to school and township elections.

rules.note: The section's heading is 'Tie vote certified by canvassing board--Automatic recount'. The kinds are a mapping of 'an office or position' [inferred].

rules.note: A recount that occurs only on a tie. The election officer recounts all ballots cast in the race and re-examines uncounted ballots; a tie that remains goes to the lot (see ties). Does not apply to a race run by instant runoff voting (pilot project).

VA.name: Virginia

code.name: Code of Virginia, Title 24.2 (Elections), and Constitution of Virginia, Article V
code.edition: the current Code as Virginia Law (the General Assembly's LIS site) prints it, pages dated 11/7/2026; 24.2-802.1 shows amendment by 2026, c. 1078

notes: Read in full from the site's chapter pages: Title 24.2 Chapter 6 (24.2-670 to 24.2-687), Chapter 8 (recounts and contests), Chapter 5 (nominations); and Article V sections 2, 13 and 15 of the Constitution of Virginia. Election contest sections of Chapter 8 (24.2-803 to 24.2-814) were read only for a tie sentence (24.2-803(H)).

There is no automatic recount in the sections read: every recount follows a defeated candidate's (or 50 voters') petition. Tie before a recount: lot (local, General Assembly, Congress, electors) or the General Assembly (Governor, with the Lieutenant Governor and Attorney General by cross-reference). Tie after a recount: a special election, except for Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General and electors.
Earlier lead 'VA lot (24.2-674)' is right for local, legislative, congressional and elector offices but does not cover the three statewide executive offices.

threshold.percent_of: the total vote cast for the two such candidates
threshold.conditions: the margin is judged on the totals as determined by the State Board or electoral board before the recount; the petition is filed within 10 days of certification (2 calendar days to 5:00 p.m. for presidential electors); the defeated candidate petitions
threshold.in_words: a margin of one-half of one percent or less of the vote for the two candidates: the defeated candidate may petition and the recount is paid by the counties and cities, not the candidate

who_may_request: the defeated candidate, by petition to the circuit court (Circuit Court of the City of Richmond for a statewide office or presidential electors; the circuit court of the county or city where the challenged candidate resides, otherwise), within 10 days after certification
rules.cost_bearer: the counties and cities comprising the election district (no bond)

sources.quote: When there is between any candidate apparently nominated or elected and any candidate apparently defeated a difference of not more than one percent of the total vote cast for the two such candidates as determined by the State Board or the electoral board, the defeated candidate may appeal from the determination of the State Board or the electoral board for a recount of the vote as set forth in this article.

Costs of the recount shall be assessed against the counties and cities comprising the election district when (i) the candidate petitioning for the recount is declared the winner; (ii) the petitioners in a recount of a referendum win the recount; or (iii) there was between the candidate apparently nominated or elected and the candidate petitioning for the recount a difference of not more than one-half of one percent of the total vote cast for the two such candidates as determined by the State Board or electoral board prior to the recount.

The petition for a recount of an election, other than an election for presidential electors, shall be filed within 10 days from the day the State Board or the electoral board certifies the result of the election

rules.note: No margin larger than one percent gives a right to a recount (next rule). A recount is judicial: a three-judge recount court, one recount per precinct, final and not appealable. For a write-in candidate apparently elected or defeated, the margin is five percent of the vote for the two candidates (24.2-800(B)).

notes: Read in full as printed: 17 V.S.A. chapter 51 (conduct of elections, including subchapter 9 recounts), chapter 49 (nominations, primary section 2369) and chapter 55 (local elections). The three chapter pages are the General Assembly's own full-text pages.

Vermont's rule is a recount by right to a losing candidate at 2 percent (5 for State Representative and local office); the State pays the recounts under chapter 51 subchapter 9; a tie leads to a recount and then a runoff election, except in a primary (party committee) and for a public question (certified not passed).

West Virginia's tie rule is the only one among my states with neither a lot nor a new election: the canvassing board, or the Governor after thirty days on a tied person's application, simply selects one of the tied persons. Its recount is a candidate's demand with no margin condition, at the candidate's cost unless the result changes.

threshold.in_words: no margin is required: a candidate may demand that the board open any of the sealed packages of ballots and recount them, within 48 hours of the declaration

who_may_request: a candidate on the ballot in entirely one county, by demand to the county board of canvassers within the 48-hour period

sources.quote: Within the 48-hour period, a candidate on the ballot in entirely one county may demand the board to open and examine any of the sealed packages of ballots and recount them.
If the result of the election is not changed by the recount, the costs and expenses of the recount shall be paid by the party at whose instance the recount was made.

Every candidate who demands a recount shall be required to furnish bond in a reasonable amount with good sufficient surety to guarantee payment of the costs and the expenses of the recount in the event the result of the election is not changed by the recount; but the amount of the bond shall in no case exceed $300.

The provisions of article six of this chapter, relating to the recount of votes in general elections, shall, to the extent applicable, be operative in primary and other elections conducted under provisions of this article.

Wyoming settles every tie by lot (county canvassing board or the state canvassing board of governor, secretary of state, auditor and treasurer), and recounts automatically at under 1% of the lowest winning candidate's votes.

threshold.percent_of: the number of votes cast for the winning candidate receiving the least number of votes cast for that office
threshold.conditions: the difference is between the winning candidate receiving the least number of votes and the losing candidate receiving the greatest number of votes (so it covers offices with several seats); the recount is of the entire district in which the candidates stand
threshold.in_words: a difference of less than one percent of the votes cast for the lowest winning candidate: all the votes for the office are recounted, with no request

rules.cost_bearer: the county in which the recount is taken, regardless of the result

sources.quote: There shall be a recount made of all the votes cast for any office in which the difference in number of votes cast for the winning candidate receiving the least number of votes and the number of votes cast for the losing candidate receiving the greatest number of votes is less than one percent (1%) of the number of votes cast for the winning candidate receiving the least number of votes cast for that office.

If the recount is initiated by the county canvassing board or required by W.S. 22-16-109(b), the cost of the recount shall be paid by the county in which the recount is taken regardless of the result of the recount.

rules.note: The text says 'any office' and does not separate federal, state, local or primary elections, so the kinds are my reading [inferred for primary and local]. A tie has a difference of zero and so meets this threshold.

rules.applies_to: a losing candidate, for the office the candidate sought

threshold.conditions: the candidate files an affidavit alleging that fraud or error occurred in counting, returning or canvassing the votes cast in any part of the district, not later than two days after the county canvass (or the state canvass, for an office the state canvassing board certifies); a deposit of $500 if the difference (computed as in 22-16-109(b)) is 1% or more but under 5%, $3,000 if 5% or more
threshold.in_words: no margin is required, but the candidate must allege fraud or error in an affidavit and post a deposit sized by the margin

who_may_request: a losing candidate, by affidavit filed in the office where the candidate filed the application for nomination, within two days after the canvass
rules.cost_bearer: the county if the recount shows sufficient error to change the result (and the deposit is returned); otherwise the requesting candidate, up to the amount deposited, per county recounted

sources.quote: There shall be a recount made of all the votes cast for any office if a losing candidate requests one under provision of W.S. 22-16-110.

A candidate may obtain a recount of votes for the office he is seeking by making and filing an affidavit alleging that fraud or error occurred in counting, returning or canvassing the votes cast in any part of the district in which he is standing for election.

If the recount shows sufficient error to change the result of the election, the county in which the recount is taken shall pay expenses of the recount and the deposit shall be returned. Otherwise the applicant or applicants seeking the recount shall be liable for the actual cost of conducting the recount up to a maximum of the amount deposited under subsection (a) of this section, per county recounted.

rules.note: A recount a candidate may buy beyond the 1% margin, on an affidavit of fraud or error and at the candidate's own cost unless the result changes.

threshold.percent_of: the total number of votes cast on the proposition (for a constitutional amendment, the total number of votes cast in the election)
threshold.conditions: measured from the number of votes required for passage: the proposition receives a number of votes, greater or lesser, within 1% of the number required
threshold.in_words: the proposition receives a number of votes, greater or lesser, within one percent of the number of votes required for passage

rules.cost_bearer: the county in which the recount is taken

sources.quote: A recount will be made if the proposition receives a number of votes, greater or lesser, within one percent (1%) of the number of votes required for passage. The one percent (1%) variance shall be calculated based upon the total number of votes cast on the proposition, except for constitutional amendments in which case the variance shall be calculated based upon the total number of votes cast in the election
The county in which the recount is taken shall pay the costs of the recount if the recount is required by subsection (a)(i) of this section

rules.note: 'Within one percent' is not stated as inclusive or exclusive, so `inclusive` is left null.

threshold.conditions: an affidavit signed by 25 electors registered in a district voting on the question, filed with the county clerk (or the secretary of state for a multi-county proposition) within two days after the canvass, with a deposit of $100
threshold.in_words: no margin is required: 25 registered electors may request a recount by affidavit with a $100 deposit

who_may_request: 25 electors registered in a district voting on the question, by affidavit
rules.cost_bearer: the signers, jointly and severally, for the cost of the recount they requested up to $500 per county recounted if the results are not changed by the recount

sources.quote: A recount will be made if requested in an affidavit signed by twenty-five (25) electors registered in a district voting on the question.

the signers of the affidavit referred to in subsection (a)(ii) of this section shall be jointly and severally liable for the costs of the recount requested by them up to five hundred dollars ($500.00) per county recounted if the results of the election are not changed by the recount.

rules.note: A recount any group of 25 electors may buy, whatever the margin.
